title: Normalized quotient comparison and ordinary finite evaluations
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf{Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site of $W$, write $R_W=\varprojlim_n S_{W,n}$ and $S_{W,n}=(A/t^{n+1})_W$ with their specified projections and quotient transitions [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. The scheme and coefficient universes are independent. Use the functors $G$, $F_W$ (reductions), $H_W$ (koszuls), $D_g$ (diagramPull), $B_g$ (finite), and the predicates BalancedNormalization, QuotientUnitNormalization, KoszulNormalization, ReductionNormalization, with their literal section formulas, from [def-a1-finite-pullback-strict-tower-data]. These act on all unbounded cochain complexes of $R_W$-module sheaves; tensor products are the sheafified tensor and their signed direct-sum totalization [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. There exists a natural isomorphism $C:F_Y\mathbin{\ggg}D_g\cong B_g$ satisfying QuotientUnitNormalization. For each $n$, there exists a unique natural isomorphism $e_n:O_{Y,n}\mathbin{\ggg}G\cong O^g_n$, where $O_{Y,n}$ is ordinary reduction restricted along the completed projection and $O^g_n$ is its ordinary finite pullback, satisfying OrdinaryNormalization and PublishedCompatibility [def-a1-completed-pullback-universe-transport-data]. Moreover, for every good complex $P$ (K-flat with flat terms [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex]), there exists a strict tower isomorphism $r:P\otimes S_{Y,\bullet}\cong\operatorname{OrdRed}(P)$ satisfying ReductionNormalization, and in every degree $i$ the level-$n$ component of $C_P$ equals $G(r_{n}^{i})$ followed by $(e_n)_{P^i}$. PublishedCompatibility is literal sectionwise conjugation to completedReductionOrdinaryComparison through a unique PublishedOrdinaryTransport for every supplied coefficient and module transport.

proof.text: The uniformizer is given by compatible constant residues. The coefficient map preserves it by equality of all limit projections. The specified completed coefficient resolution identifies each finite projection with the cokernel of the appropriate uniformizer power. Exact module inverse image preserves this cokernel. Hence the coefficient square identifies with the square of actual principal sheaf quotients.

Use normalized inverse-image tensor comparison and the principal ideal-quotient scalar associator to construct C. Compose with coefficient association to the finite target. Its local quotient-unit formula is b times the finite generator. The associator and projection transition equations give naturality in P and strict compatibility with the recorded tower transitions.

The module-level construction gives e_n. Quotient residues lift locally; restriction of pullback adjunction units and pure tensors locally generate. Therefore the unit formula determines e_n uniquely, by sheaf separation. The canonical comparison between total tensor with a degree-zero quotient and ordinary termwise scalar extension gives r: on the degree-i summand it sends x tensor z to the recorded tensor section z tensor x. Tensor balancing and the direct-sum universal property construct its inverse and prove chain and tower naturality. Both C and G(r) followed by e_n agree on these generators, so they are equal in every degree.

For arbitrary PublishedCoefficients and SectionTransport, transport the source and target tensor presentations by the supplied additive equivalences and coefficient ring equivalences. Define the source transport on a pulled quotient-unit generator by source_unit, and define the target transport on a finite tensor by target_tensor. Balancing follows from structural and projection compatibility of PublishedCoefficients; restrictions commute by the transport naturality. Inverse section equivalences give inverses. Local tensor generation proves uniqueness of both transports. On the same generators the published normalized ordinary comparison has the e_n formula, so sheaf separation gives the required literal conjugation on every section. This proves PublishedCompatibility.

theorem quotient_comparison_with_ordinary_evaluations :
    ∃ c : reductions l E Y ⋙ diagramPull l E g ≅ finite l E g,
      QuotientUnitNormalization l E g c ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, ∃! e : ordinaryReduction l E Y n ⋙ pull l E g ≅ ordinaryFinite l E g n,
        OrdinaryNormalization l E g n e ∧ PublishedCompatibility l E g n e ∧
        ∀ (P : CochainComplex (Modules l E Y) ℤ),
        integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y P →
          ∃ r : tensorReduction l E Y P ≅ ((reductionComplex l E Y).obj P).asFunctor,
            ReductionNormalization l E Y P r ∧ ∀ i : ℤ,
              (((c.hom.app P).app (op n)).f i) =
                (pull l E g).map (((r.hom.app (op n)).f i)) ≫
                  (e.hom.app (P.X i)))
